body:
## Hold

Keep this issue blocked until the maintainer reviews #2557 and the two-host comparison.
The maintainer deferred implementation until after the approved #2556 work.

## Work

Extend the batch collector design for a release gate that uses several workers.
The trusted cut runner creates the manifest before execution.
Bind each result to its run ID, commit, tree, archive SHA-256, nextest version, target, profile, selection, and partition.
Identify tests by profile, package, binary, and full test name.
Compare completed identities with the complete expected set.
Reject missing, duplicate, foreign, stale, incomplete, canceled, timed-out, and failed results.
Include the local cut steps in the same verdict.
Keep each worker's output, exit status, JUnit report, and timing records under a separate path.
Write one index and one final verdict under gate-logs/.
Keep timings.tsv compatible with seconds followed by a tab and a unique step name.
Report test duration, phase wall time, and total gate wall time separately.
Do not count summed concurrent durations as wall time.
Do not treat duplicate skipped entries in JUnit as completed tests.

Evidence: xtask/src/verdict.rs, xtask/src/lane_split.rs, xtask/src/lanes.rs, and RECOMMENDED.md section #2908.
Related: #2908 already defines batch records and one verdict.
Reuse that design where it applies.
Public reference: https://nexte.st/docs/machine-readable/junit/.

Done means: tests reject absent, duplicate, foreign, stale, failed, and incomplete records.
Equal counts with different test identities also fail.
A complete valid record set produces one verdict with all logs available.
Only that verdict can authorize the cut-tip artifact.

Part of #2557
